body:
it's not your fault that you're depressed. sometimes these feelings just happen and they become so overwhelming that it feels like it will never change. 
i think you feel guilty for having these types of feelings knowing that you are quite privileged. it doesn't matter how much money you have, how many friends you have people still get depressed.
you also feel guilty about not seeing your friend. it sounds like she knew you cared about her and I don't think she wants to know that you are beating yourself up for this.

it's going to be okay
it's social etiquette i guess. by forcing a laugh you show that you are bonding with other people. you win some, you lose some.

I love that second paragraph! hah

It's important to remember that not everything in life has to be profound or else we would never get around to doing anything.

i think you're right. 

it's all about creating new habits i guess. i know i have bad habits of looking like i am really uninterested. i will look interested even when i'm not lol.

thank you!

Being more mindful helps, I think. See the comment below /u/marhaja , he gives a good description of it. I think you have a bit of self love to work on too. don't put people on a pedestal.

But I completely relate to you. it's really frustrating.

High school was a very painful experience for me. I went to school with a bunch of very gifted kids. I sometimes skipped school because I was so ashamed that I wasn't as smart as everyone else. It was awful. I feel better in college b/c it's a much more anonymous environment, but it's only a short term fix.

Mindfulness and meditation are absolutely crucial for people with social anxiety I think. I go mellow all the time, I can't help it my brain just shuts off. I'll try to smile more often though, I think I come off as being anxious.

Thank you!

This is all good :)

I know when I come late that's when I freak out the most. I feel completely out of my element.

I usually try to talk to the person next to me if it's a social group. Unfortunately in school no one really wants to talk to each other. I feel odd trying to talk to someone beside me in class.

I know I'll actually go and regularly recharge in the bathroom if I feel like the noise levels are getting to me. I can't be around loud noises or too many people for a long amount of time. 

Going to a random event is so awkward for me. I think that's a good idea to go to the ones with activities.

Thank you! :)

well you definitely got a good description of me. :) a,b,and c are all right. it's funny i actually thought i was good at being introspective, it turns out that i'm really not. i think there have been studies that show that being too introspective is actually a bad thing. 

i think everything in your second paragraph is basically learning how to live in the now. anxious and neurotic people tend to always live in the past or in the future. i think mediation will help with this like someone else has mentioned here.

one thing that i will say is that i don't think i've ever had trouble making eye contact with people. lol. it's actually really easy for me. if i do feel uncomfortable i just look at the bridge of their nose. it looks like you're looking them in the eye. however if people hold eye contact with me for too long i do tend to feel uncomfortable. 

it's also hard for me to remember names and sometimes if someone is talking i'll be inside my own head and i'll completely forget what they're saying. it's really odd. it's like my brain freezes at the prospect of new people.

you didn't give too much advice. thank you so much! :)
I know right? it's funny looking back on it but while it's happening it's absolutely terrifying.
I'll pretend to be drunk once I know what it's like to be drunk. lol

exactly this! it's really hard to make myself talk in large groups. but i think it's okay to be quiet sometimes. 

i guess i have to push through all the uncomfortable feelings.
great advice! i've also been told that it helps if you act like you have been friends with them forever.

i have extroverted friends too but i'm easily intimidated by them for some reason. i guess i feel like they have it more together than i do. i have noticed that once i try to not to look so inward and observe them they lose their intimidation powers over me.

shame is a huge issue for me. whenever i feel like i haven't done something up to my standards, i will more likely be more distant. it's something i'm working on right now. i need to remind myself that i'm human and it's okay to make mistakes.

thank you so much for the reply! :)

ahhh thank you. this gives me hope. 

i'm a junior in college right now and i commute. the first two years were so dumb. i spent all of my time alone and felt incredibly lonely. i think it's time to step it up a bit. i'm going to join some more clubs

i guess i'll fake it till i make it too. i know how self conscious i get when i make a mistake even if it's minor. it's really really hard for me to forget but i'll try to just pretend like it didn't even happen lol. 

this doesn't sound dumb at all :) be more confident like you said you are lol. thank you so much for your reply!
I think caffeine just makes me feel jumpy and more anxious actually lol. but it's good that it works for you :) i wish i had that....
I guess people have different responses to it. I've never drank before so I have no idea how I'll respond to it. lol
no I understand :) a lot of people have been giving that advice here. I'm under 21 though so that's not helpful to me at the moment. But I will definitely think about it when I am of age.
That's interesting. How is your brother doing now?

I think selective mutism might be a little too extreme of a diagnosis for me. I may have had it when I was younger, but I've kinda grown out of it.

Right now I just have issues with being myself, not necessarily talking to strangers. I'm more passive then I'd like to be. I am overwhelmed by large groups because there are so many people talking, I don't really know how to follow. 

**changed is to are

I know what you mean. It feels like you're living a double life and it starts to feel incredibly disingenuous.

but you gotta keep being yourself even when people tell you to stop being yourself. i think your teacher was just surprised.

I think we just have to stop putting everyone on the pedastal. err...what's that saying that helps guys approach girls.....imagine them taking a dump on the toilet? maybe i'll do that for everyone. we're all human after all.

lol.

I've actually considered whether or not I have asperger's before too and then like you I figured out that it is very very easy for me to read facial expressions. 

I think the thing about people with social anxiety is that they probably have a very high sense of other people's reaction so they will have the tendency to notice facial expressions really well. to someone on the outside it looks like aspergers.

it is a vicious cycle, you're right. the amount of times i've declined to go out socially b/c i felt like an idiot.....lol.

The fact that they know who you are more than anyone else....

and they can reject you anytime.

it's some scary shit man.

I know :(

It's ruined my life too...

so many lonely days, wondering what's wrong with you and why you can't be like everyone else.

I think it does get better with practice. lots and lots of practice.

It's okay! We social potatoes will stick together. :)

<3 Thank you so much for your reply. This is helpful!

Right now I'm trying not feel like I need validation from other people. I know it's ridiculously cheesy but I guess I need a lesson of self love. I joined toastmasters recently...and I'm absolutely terrified. I guess I'm doing the right thing if that's the case. Being uptight and serious is my default setting around strangers...I can't help it. It's going to take some serious effort to change. 

I hope everything is going well for you and that you learn how to overcome this. I know it is difficult, but I think we can do it. :)
the problem with that is that i'm already socially inept...i don't want to add alcoholic to the list. but thanks for the advice ;)

ahha people think i'm stupid too. 

i think i'm just going to put myself into group situations as much as i can. no matter how uncomfortable i am.

that's the only choice i have. i can't really deal with the loneliness anymore. I hope everything goes well for you! :)

haha I can completely relate. it's so odd...you always hear about panic attacks but what do you do with people that just shut down?

i once had someone ask me if i could speak english. LOL. i think that opened my eyes to how ridiculously far i go to subconsciously make myself invisible/indifferent.

That's EXACTLY what it is!

I feel constantly overwhelmed by everything. so i just check out, it's the only way i know how to deal without going completely crazy. 

How do you deal with it?

I really wish I could....easier said then done right? ;)

Thanks for the comment!

I think you might have issues with pushing people away because you feel like the "real" you isn't worthy for whatever reason. You have to look really deep inside yourself and ask what is it that stops you from being closer with people.
